newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BSkyB and partners gear up for digital drive.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BSkyB and partners gear up for digital drive.

text.p: Pay television giant British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc on Wednesday confirmed plans to launch 200-channel digital satellite TV next year and unveiled a powerful team of allies who will help subsidise the move.
Through the system's interactive services, viewers will be able to use their remote control handsets to carry out banking transactions, book holidays and go shopping on a virtual high street.

BSkyB has recruited British Telecommunications, Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric Works Ltd of Japan as partners in a new consortium to supply services such as home shopping and home banking to satellite viewers.

British Interactive Broadcasting (BIB), the new consortium, is to provide funding of 265 million pounds ($433 million) to subsidise the retail price of digital set-top decoder boxes down to 200 pounds or less. The venture is expected to break even after five years. "Interactive TV will add a new dimension to the broadcasting revolution in Britain and Sky again is at the forefront of these exciting changes," said BSkyB chief executive Sam Chisholm.
"The range of interactive services on offer and the set top box subsidy will make this very attractive to subscribers," he added.
Rupert Gavin, British Telecom's director of multimedia services, called BIB "an important early step on the road to the information society".
BSkyB and BT will each have stakes of 32.5 percent in the BIB consortium while Midland Bank will hold 20 percent and Matsushita the remaining 15 percent.
BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is the largest shareholder, said it had ordered one million decoders -- the box needed to decipher digital signals.
The order has been divided up between four manufacturers --- Amstrad, Pace Micro Technology, Matsushita and Grundig/Hyundai.
BT's Gavin said the box, with in-built modem, was a higher specification model than had been produced in any other country.

BSkyB plans to launch its new digital satellite TV channels in spring 1998, offering pay per view sports events and films on a near video on demand basis. The interactive services are expected to come on stream later next year.
Confirmation of the digital launch gave BSkyB shares a shot in the arm. They closed 7p higher at 602.5p, extending a run of recent gains.
BSkyB, which now has 6.2 million subscribers in Britain and Ireland, said its pre-tax profit for the nine months to end-March rose to 215 million pounds, a 21 percent rise.

Share analysts said that they believed that it would take time for the interactive services to catch on. They believed that BSkyB had achieved a coup in persuading other companies to help subsidise the launch.
"The interactive services are a thing that is very nice to have rather than a must have," said one.
"The main demand will initially be for movies and sport and BSkyB will take the cream there," he added.
Digital satellite will offer viewers better picture and sound quality as well as the multitude of TV channels and range of interactive services.

BIB said it would offer a version of its online services to cable operators who plan to switch to digital. It is also in talks with a consortium involving BSkyB which is bidding for digital terrestrial licences.
The combination of Britain's leading pay television company with the dominant telephone company is certain to be examined closely by regulators.

BT's Gavin said the BIB consortium had been in protracted talks with the European Commission and telecoms watchdog Oftel and was confident that the venture would win approval without substantial change.
Oftel said it would look closely at how the venture intends to operate but that it was not its role to approve the deal.
